title: Contract Modeling Percentages and Underpayment Thresholds — Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) Payer Classes
content:
Riverbend models what each payer class should allow on an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) as a percentage of gross billed charges, and flags an underpayment only when the shortfall passes both a dollar and a percentage threshold.

| Payer class | Expected allowed percentage of charges | Underpayment threshold (USD) | Underpayment threshold (% of expected allowed) | How the payer expresses patient cost sharing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Claim | 58.5% | 25 | 2% | deductible, coinsurance and copay |
| Commercial HMO Claim | 52% | 25 | 2% | copay primarily |
| Marketplace Exchange Plan Claim | 47.5% | 25 | 2% | deductible, coinsurance and copay |
| Medicare Advantage Plan Claim | 36% | 50 | 3% | copay primarily |
| Original Medicare Claim | 31.5% | 50 | 3% | deductible and coinsurance |
| BadgerCare Plus (Wisconsin Medicaid) Claim | 24% | 50 | 3% | nominal copay |
| Wisconsin Workers' Compensation Claim | 72% | 25 | 2% | none |

**Common to every payer class**
- A payer must pay or deny a clean claim within 30 calendar days.
- A claim closes as soon as its payer balance reaches zero.

Example (hypothetical): on billed charges of 1,000.00 under a payer class modeled at 50%, the expected allowed amount would be 500.00.
